stem: A signal is modeled by S(x) = e^(3x) cos x. What is S'(x)?

rationales.A: Multiplies the derivatives of the two factors, 3e^(3x) and -sin x, instead of applying the product rule.
rationales.B: Attaches the factor 3 to the wrong term: the 3 comes from differentiating e^(3x), which multiplies cos x, not sin x.
rationales.C: Writes the derivative of e^(3x) as 3e^x, changing the exponent 3x to x, and omits the second product-rule term.
rationales.D: By the product rule with the chain rule on e^(3x): S'(x) = 3e^(3x) cos x + e^(3x)(-sin x) = e^(3x)(3 cos x - sin x).

stem: A concentration is modeled by C(x) = x^2 e^(-x). What is C'(x)?

rationales.A: By the product rule with the chain rule on e^(-x): C'(x) = 2x e^(-x) + x^2(-e^(-x)) = e^(-x)(2x - x^2).
rationales.B: Loses the negative sign from the chain rule on e^(-x) in the second product-rule term.
rationales.C: Omits the second product-rule term x^2(-e^(-x)).
rationales.D: Multiplies the derivatives of the two factors, 2x and -e^(-x), instead of applying the product rule.

stem: A response is modeled by R(x) = √(4x^2 + 9). What is R'(x)?

rationales.B: Differentiates the inner function 4x^2 as 4x instead of 8x, then simplifies (4x)/(2√(4x^2+9)).
rationales.C: By the chain rule, R'(x) = 1/(2√(4x^2+9)) times the inner derivative 8x, which simplifies to 4x/√(4x^2+9).
rationales.D: Multiplies the inner derivative 8x by √(4x^2+9) instead of by the derivative of the square root, 1/(2√(4x^2+9)).

stem: An index is modeled by G(x) = (1 + x^4)^(1/3). What is G'(x)?

rationales.A: Negates the exponent 1/3 to -1/3 instead of reducing it by 1 to -2/3 when applying the power rule.
rationales.B: Uses the exponent +2/3 instead of -2/3 after reducing the power.
rationales.D: By the chain rule, G'(x) = (1/3)(1+x^4)^(-2/3) times the inner derivative 4x^3, which is 4x^3/(3(1+x^4)^(2/3)).

stem: The boundary of a circular field satisfies x^2 + y^2 = 169. What is dy/dx at the point (5, 12)?

rationales.A: Differentiating implicitly gives 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = -x/y. At (5, 12) this is -5/12.
rationales.B: Interchanges x and y and drops the negative sign.
rationales.C: Drops the negative sign when solving for dy/dx.
rationales.D: Uses -y/x instead of -x/y, which is the reciprocal of the correct slope.

stem: A curve satisfies x^2 + y^2 = 50. What is dy/dx at the point (-1, 7)?

rationales.B: Substitutes x = -1 as if it were +1, giving -x/y = -1/7 instead of -(-1)/7 = 1/7.
rationales.C: Uses -y/x instead of -x/y: -7/(-1) = 7, the reciprocal of the correct slope.
rationales.D: Differentiating implicitly gives 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = -x/y. At (-1, 7) this is -(-1)/7 = 1/7.

stem: A curve is given by x^2 + 3xy - y^2 = 9. What is dy/dx at the point (2, 1)?

rationales.B: Differentiating gives 2x + 3y + 3x(dy/dx) - 2y(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = -(2x + 3y)/(3x - 2y). At (2, 1) this is -7/4.
rationales.C: Omits the term 3x(dy/dx) from the product rule on 3xy, leaving (2x + 3y)/(2y).
rationales.D: Loses the negative sign when moving 2x + 3y to the other side.

stem: A curve is given by 2x^2 - xy + y^2 = 8. What is dy/dx at the point (1, 3)?

rationales.A: Differentiating gives 4x - y - x(dy/dx) + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = (y - 4x)/(2y - x). At (1, 3) this is (3 - 4)/(6 - 1) = -1/5.
rationales.C: Omits the term -x(dy/dx) from the product rule on -xy, leaving 4x - y + 2y(dy/dx) = 0 and dy/dx = (y - 4x)/(2y).
rationales.D: Loses the sign when solving, giving (4x - y)/(2y - x).
